title: Up to 56% off Japan Highway Bus Fares (Selected Routes Only) @ Willer Travel
body:
Deal: Up to 56% off Japan Highway Bus Fares (Selected Routes Only) @ Willer Travel

[scrimshaw] The system doesn't appear to let you book too far in advance, can't see any options past January.
[FTTNope] Pretty common limitation in Japan in my experience
[scrimshaw] The majority of routes that these highway buses take are all covered by high speed rail. For the most popular corridor for e.g Tokyo to Osaka, Shinkansen only takes 2.5 hours (and costs 14,920 JPY), while the bus takes 7-8 hours (cost 3300 JPY).
Obviously if you are only in Japan for a 12-day holiday, it wouldn't be a good use of your time to spend half of your day on a bumpy bus ride. Unless you really enjoy sleeping on a bus (overnight) or you're really desperate to save money on transportation costs.
The most time efficient trip that I can see (and doing only very light research) is I think Ehime -> Osaka. By train this takes about 4 hours because there is no high-speed rail servicing that region, but the bus is only 1 to 2 hours extra.
[MrZ] $30 AUD seems awfully cheap for a 7-8 hour bus ride. Are they government subsidized or something?
[scrimshaw] @MrZ: From what I can tell, WILLER Group is a completely private company.
The costs are low because the operating costs are fairly low too and they have fairly high ridership.
They can't charge too much because of shinkansen being a competitor (3x faster, & super high frequency: runs once every 15 minutes)
You also have to look at airlines, a low cost carrier (Peach or Jetstar) is like 5000 JPY at most to one-way fly from Tokyo to Osaka and 1 piece of checked luggage is only like 2000 yen extra. That's around $65 AUD to fly from one city to another with 1 piece of luggage and 7KG carryon.
Flying however is the least convenient since airports are usually located a fair ways away from large city centers.
[altomic] Intercity buses are a cool way to see everyday Japan. I’ve used them extensively.
[donga100] FYI for those considering it, these buses are often 3x slower or worse than bullet train. They are much cheaper though and an overnight bus skips a night of accommodation if you are desperate to save money.
[SilenceMinion] Feels like a nice way to see the countryside and save money (having done the Shinkansen to death). I'd have to get a window seat and hope it's not fully booked though so I can stand up when I want).
[vSchweetz] Today I learnt that Kanto is a real region…
